newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance firms say no major liquidity problem.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance firms say no major liquidity problem.

text.p: The Thai Finance Companies Association denied on Thursday market rumours that local finance firms faced a severe liquidity crunch.
President of the association, Pin Chakkapak, told reporters that he had checked the financial positions of finance companies and found that the talk was false.
"It is what the (stock) investors have interpreted and we do not have any measures to counter the rumours," he said.
The bourse hit a 56-month-low on Thursday on worries about finance firms and the baht's weakness and its effect on listed companies with U.S.-dollar denominated loans.

Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said earlier on Thursday that his bank had directed at least one small finance firm that was hit by short-term liquidity problems to restructure its capital. He did not elaborate.
Some small Thai finance companies have lately faced short term liquidity problems following sustained high domestic interest rates which have raised their funding costs, analysts said.
